$comment: Automation identity role map: the single source read by bicep/main.bicep (loadJsonContent), terraform/s3-automation-identity.tf (jsondecode) and automation/shared/scripts/NIC26.AutomationIdentity.ps1 (Test-NIC26AutomationIdentityRoles). scope = a key of the names catalog (rg_azl, rg_sec, kv_azl, kv_ops). role = a key of builtInRoles in bicep/modules/built-in-roles.bicep (the role definition IDs live there only); role_display_names maps each key to the built-in role name (Terraform role_definition_name, the PowerShell check). feature: core = Arc registration (OEM image, Invoke-AzStackHciArcInitialization) + cluster deployment with Local Identity and Key Vault; simplified_provisioning = os-provisioning/bicep/main.bicep. delegable_roles = the ABAC condition: the identity may assign or remove only these roles, only to service principals, never to itself. granted_by_s3 = the landing zone S3 security stage already grants it to the deployment identity (names.id_deploy), so IaC skips it for that identity.

assignments.purpose: Arc registration of the nodes (Invoke-AzStackHciArcInitialization): create the Microsoft.HybridCompute/machines resources in the cluster resource group
Arc registration: manage the Arc machines and install the mandatory Azure Local extensions

Cluster deployment: clusters, deploymentSettings, edgeDevices, edgeMachines, custom location, resource bridge; its built-in condition lets it assign only the Azure Local service roles (Device Management, Connected InfraVMs, Connected Machine Resource Manager, Key Vault Secrets/Certificates roles) that cluster-deploy/bicep/main.bicep assigns to the node Arc identities
Cluster deployment: read the Arc machines, the witness account and the deployment state
Cluster deployment: create the Key Vault audit-log storage account (st_diag) with its lifecycle rule; read the cloud witness key (Set-ClusterDeploymentSecrets.ps1)
Cluster deployment: the CanNotDelete lock on the audit-log storage account (template: 'an LRS account with a lock'); only Owner, User Access Administrator or a lock role may write locks

Nested deployments into the security resource group (cluster-deploy key-vault-access module, os-provisioning key-vault-delegation module) and the Key Vault audit diagnostic setting to st_diag (the storage destination's listKeys right comes from Storage Account Contributor on rg_azl); the vault lives outside the cluster resource group (design section 5.2)
Local Identity with Key Vault: assign Key Vault Secrets Officer and Certificates Officer on the cluster vault to the node Arc identities
Write the deployment secrets (<cluster>-LocalAdminCredential, <cluster>-WitnessStorageKey) and the provisioning administrator secret into the cluster vault
Manage the cluster vault resource (public network access toggle in Set-ClusterVaultPublicAccess.ps1); the vault itself is created by the landing zone
Read the node local-administrator and BMC credentials from the operations vault (the source the deployment secrets are copied from); never writes

Simplified machine provisioning: Microsoft.Edge sites, site configurations and configuration references, edge machines (Learn: Owner, or Contributor plus Role Based Access Control Administrator on the resource group)

Simplified machine provisioning: the template gives each edge machine identity a constrained Role Based Access Control Administrator on the resource group and the Azure Local resource provider app Azure Connected Machine Resource Manager; constrained to those two roles, service principals only, never itself

Simplified machine provisioning: the template gives each edge machine identity a constrained Role Based Access Control Administrator on the cluster vault (limited to Key Vault Secrets User); constrained to that one role, service principals only, never itself
